More shots on goal

In Vancouver, the cost of living keeps a lot of people from ever trying their idea. The rent gets paid first, and the idea gets whatever time is left over.

Basecamp pairs a program with affordable housing, and together they give you breathing room and a safety net to take your shot. For four to six weeks you live and work in the same place, next to other people building their own things, with one clear target: take your idea as far as you can, ideally to a first working version (a v1, or MVP: a first version that real people can use), and show what you built to your peers.

Think about why hackathons work. Everyone puts down the rest of their life for a weekend, works hard on one thing, gets feedback right away, and ends with something real. The energy does most of the work. Basecamp asks what it would look like to live inside that for four to six weeks, and how you could keep that energy and support going, in a form that fits your everyday life, after you leave.

Cohort 1 is the first season of the program, and we are building it alongside the people in it.

More people taking more shots is the point.

What you get

The program and the affordable housing work together. They give you the time and the room to build. Your residency includes:

A coworking room for residents only

Open 9am to 5pm. After 5pm there are several other places around the hostel to work.

A weekly rhythm

Each week has a standup (a short meeting where everyone says what they are working on and what is in their way), critique sessions where residents give each other direct feedback, a public progress post from every resident, and a Family Dinner at one long table. Family Dinner is pot-luck. Martin hosts, and everyone brings a dish that shares a piece of their culture or their favourite food.

Peers building very different things

Writers, developers, artists, founders and organizers in the same rooms. The mix is deliberate. A view from outside your field can be the most useful feedback you get.

Time with the founder

Martin works directly with each resident during their stay.

You own what you make

Residents own 100% of the intellectual property they create. Basecamp takes no ownership and no equity in any resident's project or venture.

A demo of what you built

Every stay ends with a demo: you show what you made to the other residents and invited guests, then hear what they think. Show it in whatever form fits your work, such as a walkthrough, a reading, a screening or a performance.

Your own way of working

Choose any tools you like, or none. Using AI is not required. You decide how you work.

Food, at lower cost

Residents buy their own groceries. We provide a guide to low-cost, high-quality food, and group buying brings the cost down further.

An HI Canada membership

A membership is included with your stay. It comes with hundreds of member discounts across Canada.

A bed in a shared pod

A pod is a section of the dorm with its own privacy enclosure. At Basecamp, two residents share each one.

What you keep

A demo of what you built, a weekly habit of showing your work, and a group of people who have seen it take shape.

Being finalized

Mentor office hours (scheduled time with an experienced mentor) are planned for the program. We are confirming mentors now and will name them here once they have agreed. We will add other perks the same way, once they are confirmed.

How a residency runs

Each resident arrives on their own date and works on their own project. You join a house that is already in motion.

  1. 1

    Arrive

    Settle into your pod, meet the people already here, and write down what you will build: a new idea, or the next stage of a project you already have. Then write the first working version of it in one sentence. That means the smallest version that really works.

  2. 2

    Build

    Work in the coworking room. Talk to the people your project is for. Share your progress publicly every week.

  3. 3

    Get feedback

    Take part in the weekly critique sessions with your peers.

  4. 4

    Demo

    Finish by showing what you built to the other residents and invited guests, and hear what they think.

A stay is four to six weeks. Cohort 1 began on October 1, 2026 and runs until April 28, 2027. Cohort 1 is testing all of this, and the program will change as we learn from each cohort.

Who Basecamp is for

Basecamp is for people who come to build.

Start a project from scratch, build on one you already have, or take an idea toward a shipped product. You go from your idea as far as you can take it in four to six weeks, ideally to a first working version: a v1, or MVP (a first version that real people can use).

You will feel at home here if:

  • You know what you want to build: a new idea, or an existing project you want to take further. You can describe, in one sentence, the working version you want by the end of your stay.
  • You have finished things before: a product, a book, a film, a piece of software, a business, a community. Tell us what, and link to it.
  • You are a founder, writer, designer, artist, developer, civic technologist or organizer, working on something of your own.
  • You can give the project your full-time attention for your whole stay.
  • You are willing to show your work publicly every week and to take honest feedback from peers.
  • You like working beside people who are building very different things.
  • You are coming on your own or with a team of any size.

The question that decides it: what will you build here, and how far can you take it in four to six weeks?

The program and affordable housing together give you the time to build. The building is why you come.

What we look for

We read every application. These are the things we look at.

A clear project

New or existing, tell us what you will build and what its first working version looks like.

A record of finishing things

Tell us what you have shipped before. Links help.

Time and commitment

Your full-time attention for your stay, and a public progress update every week.

Fit for a shared house

Residents share pods, a kitchen and a coworking room. We look for people who give feedback as well as take it.

Range

Basecamp is deliberately cross-disciplinary, so we value applicants from different fields.

Who can apply

Anyone 18 or older. You can apply alone or as a team of any size.

Immigration

Neither Basecamp nor HI Canada can help you get a visa, permit or any other immigration document. If you are coming from outside Canada, you are responsible for making sure you are allowed to be in Canada for the length of your stay. Check with the Government of Canada or a licensed immigration professional before you apply.

Tools you can use

Four tools Martin has built, which residents can use during their stay. None are required. You choose your own tools.

We Can Just Build Things

wecanjustbuildthings.dev

A catalog of over 1,300 verified tools, and a Build Studio that turns a project description into a suggested set of tools, instructions for a coding assistant, and a starter code folder.

Builder Workshop

builderworkshop.ca

A practical map and directory of British Columbia's innovation ecosystem: the organizations and venues where builders meet, and pathways for finding the right ones.

BC AI Compass

bc-aicompass.ca

A verified map and directory of British Columbia's AI ecosystem. Every entry links to the source it was checked against. Built by Martin Montero in collaboration with BC+AI.

Founder's Quest

play.foundersquest.ca

An interactive startup validation tool that guides founders through eight stages of problem research, prototyping, testing and launch, using evidence tiers and mythic storytelling.

A beachside home base
built for focus

HI Jericho Beach is part of HI Canada (Hostelling International). The heritage building was built in 1934 as barracks for the Royal Canadian Air Force and sits in parkland by Jericho Beach in Kitsilano. In summer it operates as a public hostel. We have secured two large dorm rooms exclusively for Basecamp residents.

The rooms have privacy-enclosed pods that normally accommodate four people. For Basecamp, only two people share each pod, which gives you real personal space inside a communal setting.

The building has a shared kitchen with full cooking facilities, several lounge and common areas, a home theatre for screenings and presentations, free Wi-Fi, on-site laundry and secure storage. The beach is a four-minute walk away, UBC and downtown are a short bus ride, and all major transit is close.

About Basecamp

Basecamp is a live-in residency for entrepreneurs, creators and community builders at HI Jericho Beach in Vancouver. Residents stay four to six weeks to take an idea as far as they can, ideally to a first working version, with peers beside them and a demo at the end. The structure draws on the PIE Cookbook, an open-source playbook for community-driven programs from the Portland Incubator Experiment.

How the program is designed: Our Model

Where it comes from

In 2014, Martin founded Startup Basecamp: Philly. He turned a former halfway house in Philadelphia's Brewerytown neighbourhood, just outside Girard College, into shared living for social entrepreneurs, creatives and local craftspeople. It was the second Startup Basecamp location in the country and the first shared living space of its kind in Philadelphia.

Read the original story in Generocity

Basecamp in Vancouver continues that work.

Martin Montero, Founder & Director

Martin has spent fifteen years building community spaces for people who make things, across four countries. He was a member of the founding team for the Impact Hub expansion into the United States (Impact Hub is a global network of community spaces) and a founding member of Bootstrap Austin. In 2014 he founded Startup Basecamp: Philly, and he is Founder & Director of Basecamp in Vancouver. Today he is part of AOS, a freedom-tech collective, and DCTRL, Vancouver's decentralized-tech space. He built Basecamp to give more people the room to take a shot at their idea.

Questions

How long is a stay?

Four to six weeks. You arrive on your own date.

What is the last date I can arrive?

Stays finish by April 28, 2027. For a six-week stay, the last arrival date is March 17, 2027. For a four-week stay, it is March 31, 2027.

Who can apply?

Anyone 18 or older, from Vancouver or anywhere else. You can apply alone or as a team of any size.

Can my teammates and I share a pod?

Yes, if a full pod is available. Beds are assigned at check-in based on what is available that day.

Can you help with a visa?

No. Neither Basecamp nor HI Canada can help with visas, permits or any other immigration document. If you are coming from outside Canada, you are responsible for making sure you are allowed to be in Canada for the length of your stay.

Do I have to use AI?

No. You choose your own tools, including none at all.

What does the $600 a month cover?

Per resident: your bed in a shared pod, utilities, Wi-Fi, the shared kitchen, lounges, home theatre, secure storage, the residents-only coworking room, the weekly program, time with the founder, your demo and an HI Canada membership. Food and laundry are not included.

How do I book and pay?

Bookings and payments are handled by the HI Jericho Beach front desk. A stay of four weeks pays the full $600 CAD. Stays longer than a month continue at $20 CAD a day.

What if I need to cancel?

Cancellations and refunds are available only in emergencies.

Who owns what I make?

You do. Residents own 100% of the intellectual property they create. Basecamp takes no ownership and no equity in any resident's project or venture.

Do I buy my own food?

Yes. Residents buy their own groceries. We provide a guide to low-cost, high-quality food, and group buying brings the cost down further.

What is Family Dinner?

A weekly pot-luck at one long table. Martin hosts, and everyone brings a dish that shares a piece of their culture or their favourite food.

Where do I sleep?

In a pod at HI Jericho Beach, shared with one other resident. Beds are assigned at check-in based on what is available that day.

When can I use the coworking room?

It is for Basecamp residents only and is open 9am to 5pm. After 5pm there are several other places around the hostel to work.

How much time does Basecamp ask for?

Your full-time attention for the whole stay, a public progress update every week, and your part in the weekly critique sessions.

Who sees my demo?

The other residents and invited guests. You can show it in whatever form fits your work.

How do I apply?

Fill in the form below. Tell us what you are building and what its first working version looks like.
